Issues.Title: Stop build-failure-analysis workflows from filing a public detection-runs issue
Issues.Body:
Addresses https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/55753#issuecomment-5272285880 — stop the build-failure-analysis workflows from filing a public issue.

## Problem

Two problems, and the second is worse than the one originally reported.

**1. Public noise.** `[aw] Detection Runs` (#55753) is a **public** issue in this repo, and every comment Build Failure Analysis posted to it was `reason: parse_error` — never a real finding.

**2. Threat detection silently discards the entire analysis.** `safe_outputs` is hard-gated:

```yaml
if: (!cancelled()) && needs.agent.result != 'skipped' && needs.detection.result == 'success'
```

Any detection-job failure therefore drops the PR comment and inline suggestions on the floor. That is not hypothetical — it is what happened in the run behind the first tracking comment, [31630918989](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/actions/runs/31630918989): `agent` succeeded, `detection` **failed**, and `safe_outputs` was **skipped**. The build owner got no analysis at all.

## Root cause of the `parse_error`

From the `detection` job log of that run — the detection model never ran:

```
Downloading checksums from https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/releases/download/v1.0.70/SHA256SUMS.txt...
curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 503
curl: (56) Connection died, tried 5 times before giving up
##[error]Process completed with exit code 56
...
sudo: awf: command not found
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1
...
Detection log stats: 2 lines, 29 bytes
##[error]Failed to parse detection result: No THREAT_DETECTION_RESULT found in detection log.
```

A transient **HTTP 503** from the release CDN meant the Copilot CLI was never installed, so `awf` was missing, so the detection engine never executed, so its log was empty (29 bytes) and there was no `THREAT_DETECTION_RESULT` to parse. `parse_error` is the *symptom*; the cause is infrastructure flake during CLI install — not a prompt or model problem, and not a missing token.

**`continue-on-error: true` does not protect against this.** It is already the default here, but `parse_threat_detection_results.cjs` only takes the warn path when the engine actually ran:

```js
if (continueOnError && !detectionExecutionFailed) { /* warning */ }
else { core.setFailed(msg); }
```

With `DETECTION_AGENTIC_EXECUTION_OUTCOME=failure` it goes to `setFailed`, the job fails, and the gate above skips all safe outputs. So detection is a single point of failure that converts any transient infra hiccup into total, silent loss of output.

## Why disabling is the available lever

In gh-aw **v0.82.9** there is no way to keep detection while suppressing the issue or relaxing the gate:

- [`buildConclusionDetectionRunsStep`](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/blob/v0.82.9/pkg/workflow/notify_comment_conclusion_helpers.go) emits `Log detection run` whenever `IsDetectionJobEnabled` is true — it takes no other input.
- The `threat-detection` schema accepts only `enabled`, `prompt`, `steps`, `post-steps`, `runs-on`, `engine`, `max-ai-credits`, `continue-on-error`. None opt out of the issue.
- [`handle_detection_runs.cjs`](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/blob/v0.82.9/actions/setup/js/handle_detection_runs.cjs) hardcodes `context.repo`, so it cannot be pointed at a private repo.
- The `needs.detection.result == 'success'` gate is emitted identically by v0.84.4 (see `issue-monster`, `issue-triage`, `parallel-safety-audit-command`), so a compiler bump alone does not fix the blocking behaviour.

What actually bounds these workflows is unchanged: the agent never writes to GitHub directly, and the safe-outputs handler only permits comments in this repository.

## Note on the duplicated key

`threat-detection: false` is declared in **both** the shared file and `build-failure-analysis-command.md` because it **cannot be inherited**. It parses to a nil config, and the import merge in `mergeImportedSafeOutputs` guards on `importedConfig.ThreatDetection != nil`, so a disabled detection arriving from an import is silently dropped and the workflow falls back to the auto-default (enabled). Verified: removing the restatement puts the `detection` job and its `Log detection run` step straight back into `build-failure-analysis-command.lock.yml`. Both sites are marked KEEP IN SYNC.

## Changes

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `shared/build-failure-analysis-shared.md` | `threat-detection: false` + rationale; corrected a now-stale `needs: [activation, agent, detection]` comment |
| `build-failure-analysis-command.md` | Restated `threat-detection: false` (cannot be inherited) |
| both `.lock.yml` | Regenerated |

This is the only functional change — `report-failure-as-issue: false` and `noop.report-as-issue: false` were already on `main` and are untouched.

## Validation

- Lock files regenerated with `gh aw compile --strict` using gh-aw **v0.82.9**, matching the `compiler_version` already in their metadata — no compiler bump smuggled in. Recompile is idempotent.
- Absent from both locks: the `detection` job, `Log detection run`, `handle_detection_runs`, `needs.detection`, `GH_AW_THREAT_DETECTION`.
- Intact: `add_comment` and `create_pull_request_review_comment`; `safe_outputs` `needs` correctly reduced to `[activation, agent]` and no longer gated on detection.
- No other workflow's lock file was touched.

## Follow-up

Five other workflows still run detection (`issue-monster`, `issue-monster-assigner`, `issue-triage`, `add-tactics-template-on-comment`, `parallel-safety-audit-command`), so #55753 can still receive comments from them — and by the same gate, each is exposed to losing its safe outputs on a transient detection failure. Worth raising upstream with gh-aw: a detection **infrastructure** failure should be distinguishable from a detection **verdict**, and `continue-on-error: true` should keep safe outputs flowing in the former case. Once that exists, detection can be re-enabled here.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Stop build-failure-analysis workflows from filing a public detection-runs issue" (#55771)

Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git and Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. Improper removal of sensitive information before storage or transfer in .NET allows an unauthorized attacker to disclose information over a network. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/sourcelink/issues/1757 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Medium - **Score:** 5.9 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-212: Improper Removal of Sensitive Information Before Storage or Transfer ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects any Microsoft .NET project if it uses any of affected package versions listed below ### Published NuGet packages Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git) | = 8.0.0 | No patched NuGet version; update to a fixed .NET 8 SDK [Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git) | >= 10.0.102, <= 10.0.110 | 10.0.111 [Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git) | >= 10.0.200, <= 10.0.204 | No patched NuGet version; the 10.0.2xx SDK feature band is no longer serviced [Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git) | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.301 | 10.0.303 [Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git) | = 8.0.0 | No patched NuGet version; update to a fixed .NET 8 SDK [Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git) | >= 10.0.102, <= 10.0.110 | 10.0.111 [Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git) | >= 10.0.200, <= 10.0.204 | No patched NuGet version; the 10.0.2xx SDK feature band is no longer serviced [Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git) | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.301 | 10.0.303 The affected packages used by .NET 8 and .NET 9 SDKs are built with SDK-specific prerelease versions that aren't published as stable NuGet packages. Update to SDK 8.0.130 or 8.0.424, SDK 9.0.120 or 9.0.317, or SDK 10.0.111 or 10.0.303 to receive the fix. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Windows Presentation Foundation. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-50648 | .NET Denial of Service Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET XML Encryption (System.Security.Cryptography.Xml). This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. A denial of service vulnerability exists in the XML encryption implementation (EncryptedXml) in .NET 8, .NET 9, and .NET 10. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by supplying crafted encrypted XML that causes uncontrolled resource consumption, resulting in denial of service. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/130714 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.5 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-770 (Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** All - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects any Microsoft .NET project if it uses any of affected package versions listed below ### .NET 10.0 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [System.Security.Cryptography.Xml](https://www.nuget.org/packages/System.Security.Cryptography.Xml) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.9 | 10.0.10 ### .NET 9.0 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [System.Security.Cryptography.Xml](https://www.nuget.org/packages/System.Security.Cryptography.Xml) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.17 | 9.0.18 ### .NET 8.0 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [System.Security.Cryptography.Xml](https://www.nuget.org/packages/System.Security.Cryptography.Xml) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.3 | 8.0.4 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? To update the System.Security.Cryptography.Xml NuGet package, use one of the following methods: NuGet Package Manager UI in Visual Studio: - Open your project in Visual Studio. - Right-click on your project in Solution Explorer and select "Manage NuGet Packages..." or navigate to "Project > Manage NuGet Packages". - In the NuGet Package Manager window, select the "Updates" tab. This tab lists packages with available updates from your configured package sources. - Select the package(s) you wish to update. You can choose a specific version from the dropdown or update to the latest available version. - Click the "Update" button. Using the NuGet Package Manager Console in Visual Studio: - Open your project in Visual Studio. - Navigate to "Tools > NuGet Package Manager > Package Manager Console". - To update a specific package to its latest version, use the following Update-Package command: ```Update-Package -Id System.Security.Cryptography.Xml``` Using the .NET CLI (Command Line Interface): - Open a terminal or command prompt in your project's directory. - To update a specific package to its latest version, use the following add package command: ```dotnet add package System.Security.Cryptography.Xml``` Once you have updated the nuget package reference you must recompile and deploy your application. Additionally we recommend you update your runtime and/or SDKs, but it is not necessary to patch the vulnerability. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-50527 | .NET Denial of Service Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET XML Encryption (System.Security.Cryptography.Xml). This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. A denial of service vulnerability exists in the XML encryption implementation (EncryptedXml) in .NET 8, .NET 9, and .NET 10. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by supplying crafted encrypted XML that is improperly validated, resulting in denial of service. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/130712 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.5 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-121 (Stack-based Buffer Overflow) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** All - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects any Microsoft .NET project if it uses any of affected package versions listed below ### .NET 10.0 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [System.Security.Cryptography.Xml](https://www.nuget.org/packages/System.Security.Cryptography.Xml) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.9 | 10.0.10 ### .NET 9.0 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [System.Security.Cryptography.Xml](https://www.nuget.org/packages/System.Security.Cryptography.Xml) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.17 | 9.0.18 ### .NET 8.0 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [System.Security.Cryptography.Xml](https://www.nuget.org/packages/System.Security.Cryptography.Xml) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.3 | 8.0.4 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? To update the System.Security.Cryptography.Xml NuGet package, use one of the following methods: NuGet Package Manager UI in Visual Studio: - Open your project in Visual Studio. - Right-click on your project in Solution Explorer and select "Manage NuGet Packages..." or navigate to "Project > Manage NuGet Packages". - In the NuGet Package Manager window, select the "Updates" tab. This tab lists packages with available updates from your configured package sources. - Select the package(s) you wish to update. You can choose a specific version from the dropdown or update to the latest available version. - Click the "Update" button. Using the NuGet Package Manager Console in Visual Studio: - Open your project in Visual Studio. - Navigate to "Tools > NuGet Package Manager > Package Manager Console". - To update a specific package to its latest version, use the following Update-Package command: ```Update-Package -Id System.Security.Cryptography.Xml``` Using the .NET CLI (Command Line Interface): - Open a terminal or command prompt in your project's directory. - To update a specific package to its latest version, use the following add package command: ```dotnet add package System.Security.Cryptography.Xml``` Once you have updated the nuget package reference you must recompile and deploy your application. Additionally we recommend you update your runtime and/or SDKs, but it is not necessary to patch the vulnerability. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-47300 | .NET Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in ASP.NET Core Negotiate Authentication (Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.Negotiate). This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. An elevation of privilege vulnerability exists in the ASP.NET Core Negotiate authentication handler in .NET 8, .NET 9, and .NET 10 due to improper validation. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/67785 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.8 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-303 (Incorrect Implementation of Authentication Algorithm) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** All - **Architectures:** All ### Mitigation Factors Your ASP.NET Core app is only affected if it uses Negotiate authentication and LDAP to retrieve role information. ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects any Microsoft .NET project if it uses any of affected package versions listed below ### .NET 10.0 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.Negotiate](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.Negotiate) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.9 | 10.0.10 ### .NET 9.0 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.Negotiate](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.Negotiate) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.17 | 9.0.18 ### .NET 8.0 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.Negotiate](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.Negotiate) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.28 | 8.0.29 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. If your application references the vulnerable nuget package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. * If you're using .NET 8.0, you should download and install .NET 8.0.29 Runtime or .NET 8.0.129 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/8.0. * If you're using .NET 9.0, you should download and install .NET 9.0.18 Runtime or .NET 9.0.316 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/9.0. * If you're using .NET 10.0, you should download and install .NET 10.0.10 Runtime or .NET 10.0.302 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/10.0. Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect. Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind.
